title: Next-token loss and perplexity
goal:
A language model factorizes $p(x)$ into next-token conditionals (Section 2, Equation 1). Training minimizes the average negative log-probability of each token given the tokens before it, and perplexity is the exponential of that average (Section 3.1).

Write two functions:

- `lm_loss(logits, tokens)` takes `logits` of shape `(T, V)` and an integer array `tokens` of length `T`. Row `t` of `logits` is the model's prediction for the token at position `t + 1`, made after reading tokens `0` to `t`. Return the mean negative log-probability, in nats, over the `T - 1` predictions that have a target.
- `perplexity(logits, tokens)` returns `exp(lm_loss(...))`.

The starter includes the signatures. You write a numerically stable log-softmax inside `lm_loss`.
hints: Row `t` predicts `tokens[t + 1]`, so drop the last row of `logits` and the first entry of `tokens`.
`log_softmax(z) = z - max(z) - log(sum(exp(z - max(z))))`. Subtracting the maximum keeps `exp` from overflowing when logits are around 1000.
Pick each target's log-probability with `logp[np.arange(T - 1), tokens[1:]]`, negate it, and take the mean.
Perplexity uses the natural logarithm's inverse, `np.exp`, not `2 **`, because the loss is in nats.
